big_case.notes: Substantial border-construction, conservation, and historic-resource interests, with a significant clarification of the statutory-versus-constitutional review boundary. This remains an interim stay rather than final adjudication of all challenges to the waiver program.

leakage.notes: All nine calls have captured results according to the log. Their queries read the prediction contract, provisioned arrival inputs, application, statpack, schemas, and generated artifacts; no external case-specific retrieval or outcome-file read appears. The rationale consistently treats the case as unresolved. The October 23 prediction precedes the November 9 stay grant.

central_claims.basis: The November 9 order stays the district-court injunction without a geographic carveout, pending a timely certiorari petition; it does not summarily reverse.
central_claims.claim: The full Court will grant an unqualified stay of the entire injunction, rather than carve out the National Park or immediately summarily reverse.

central_claims.basis: The per curiam adopts precisely this distinction and cites Dalton v. Specter, which the forecast specifically identified.
central_claims.claim: The major-questions theory cannot convert a statutory-authority challenge into a constitutional claim permitted by section 102(c)(2)(A).

central_claims.basis: The per curiam finds unrecoverable construction costs and border-security harm, and holds that Congress's statutory balance outweighs the respondents' asserted injuries.
central_claims.claim: Government construction and border interests will prevail in the balance of equities.

central_claims.basis: The docket records a response request on October 22, the FAIR amicus filing on October 29, and referral on November 9.
central_claims.claim: The application will receive a response request, full-Court referral, and at least one amicus filing before disposition.
